title: docs(app-shell): record why client Zod issues are advisory at the Save gate, and pin the asymmetry (#6980)
body:
Part of #6980 — the card asked for a verdict between two readings, and named a small deliverable for one of them. This PR is that deliverable. Accepting the verdict is still the PM's, so this does not close the card.

## Verdict: reading (1), with one correction the evidence forces

The card's reading (1) was "the suppression is deliberate and merely undocumented". Measured, its **substance holds and its wording does not**:

- **Advisory is the correct behaviour.** Supported, and the reason is sharper than "spec skew might happen" — see below.
- **It was never argued at the Save gate.** The card's reading (2) is right about that, and it is the reason the comment was missing. So the suppression is not a decision taken at the gate; it is the unstated consequence of a principle this module states and enforces in five other places.

Reading (2)'s *diagnosis* is therefore correct and its *prescribed fix* is not. That is what this PR records, so the next reader gets both halves.

## The discriminator the card was missing: whether the server backstops the class

- **Inspector issues have no backstop.** #4306 measured `record.est_hours *` saving with a 200 and a success toast, and publishing made the malformed expression the live field definition. The runtime authoring gate reports its findings only as *advisory*, on an already-**successful** save (#4133 → `metadataClientFactory.onSaveAdvisory`). The client is the only gate, so it must block.
- **Schema issues do have one.** `saveMetaItem` runs the same contract, and `doSave` already maps the refusal — `422` / `INVALID_METADATA` / `INVALID_PAYLOAD` — straight back into the same inline `issues` (`ResourceEditPage.tsx`, the catch block in `doSave`). `clientValidation.ts`'s own header says as much: the live pass exists so authors "no longer have to wait for the next save round-trip". A schema-invalid draft cannot land. The client Zod pass is a **preview of the server's verdict**, not the thing standing between the draft and storage.

So gating Save on Zod adds no protection. The only thing it can add is the one failure the client can cause on its own: being **stricter** than the server.

## The skew class is real, and the root-cure covers one sixth of it

`validateMetadataDraft`'s `serverSchema` cure suppresses exactly: a **top-level** issue (`path.length === 1`) on a field **absent** from the draft that the live server marks optional. Measured on the bundled `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0, here is where the other classes land:

| skew class | issue arrives at | cure applies |
|---|---|---|
| top-level required, absent, server-optional | `path.length 1` | **yes** |
| server gains a root key | `unrecognized_keys`, `path.length 0` | no |
| server gains a nested key | `unrecognized_keys`, `path.length 2` (e.g. `nodes.0`) | no |
| nested required key | `path.length 3` (e.g. `nodes.0.label`) | no |
| present-but-invalid (format / enum / narrowed union) | any depth, field present | no, by design |
| enum member added server-side | `invalid_value` | only flow `nodes.N.type`, via a 2-entry hard-coded set |

**14 of the 15 wired root schemas reject an undeclared key.** So the single most likely forward skew — the running server gains one authorable key — is uncovered on almost every type.

And it is not hypothetical. objectstack#5316 is a landed instance of exactly it: stored `view` bodies carry `isPinned` / `sortOrder`, written by the platform's own pin and reorder actions, and the authoring schema rejected them. `clientValidation.ts` records the verdict in its own words — *"Judging a stored body by the authoring schema made the client strictly stricter than the server."* Under today's advisory gate that cost a false banner. Under a blocking gate it would have dead-bolted Save for every author who had ever pinned a view, on a body the server accepts, with no on-screen editor able to take `isPinned` back out — the pin lives in the view switcher, not the form.

That wedge is the hazard every gate in this family is explicitly built around: `blockingReport`'s selection stamp, and its siblings in `ObjectFieldInspector`, `ConditionBuilder`, `ConditionalFormattingEditor` and `PermissionAdvancedFacets`. A blocking Zod gate would have reintroduced it in the one form no editor can clear.

## What is here

- **`ResourceEditPage.tsx` — comments only.** 48 added lines, 0 removed, every added line a comment (proved by filtering the diff). The rationale sits once at `blockingReport`, where the existing #4306 comment states the blocking half; a four-line pointer sits at the Save button's `disabled` expression, which is where someone would go to "fix" this.
- **`ResourceEditPage.schemaAdvisory.test.tsx`** — pins both halves against **one** draft, so the asymmetry itself is the assertion. The fixture is the real skew shape: the stored page carries an undeclared root key, and the mocked type entry hands the validator a maximally lenient server schema (`required: []`) — a server that requires nothing at all — and the client still rejects, because `unrecognized_keys` has an empty path. No server hint can rescue this class.
- **Empty-frontmatter changeset**, declared as releasing nothing.

## Reverse verification — and it caught my own test first

Predicted in writing before running: wiring `issues.length > 0` into the Save gate should turn the suite red.

**First run, against the suite as first written: 1 failed / 2 — and it failed on the wrong assertion.** The "Save stays enabled" half **passed** under the mutation, because `waitFor(() => expect(save).toBeEnabled())` retries and had succeeded on a render taken before the 200 ms-debounced `issues` landed. The mutation was only caught incidentally, by a `title` assertion in the second test. The pin was vacuous exactly where it mattered.

Fixed by anchoring on the banner — which proves the validator ran on *this* draft and rejected it — and then asserting Save's state **synchronously**, with no retry window.

**Second run, same mutation: 2 failed / 2**, both on the designed assertion, `Received element is not enabled` with `disabled="" title="Save (⌘S)"`.

Mutation and restore were both proved on disk, not from an exit code: target blob `2a3d0722` → `a76b75e9` → `2a3d0722` (equal to the `HEAD` blob), occurrences of the old text 1 → 0 → 1 and of the injected text 0 → 1 → 0, and `git diff HEAD` empty after restore. The script restores via `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap. No `dist` is involved: the suite imports `./ResourceEditPage` by relative path, i.e. source.

## Verification

All at `38f493109`, the final commit. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013hfmP9hoMd3dJwTh85J4yB

- **New suite:** `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 2 passed (2)` — 1 path passed in, 1 file reported.
- **Regression:** the 10 neighbouring suites (`ResourceEditPage.celGate`, `.defaultGate`, and all seven `clientValidation.*`) plus the new one — 10 paths passed in, `Test Files 10 passed (10)` / `Tests 134 passed (134)`.
- **`pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check`** (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) — exit 0, with the script name echoed so this is not a zero-match silent pass. The main tsconfig **excludes** `**/*.test.tsx`, so that pass says nothing about the new file; `tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` confirms it is in the program (1 hit, against a `celGate` control also at 1).
- **eslint, plain form**, `--format json`: new test file `errors=0 warnings=0`; `ResourceEditPage.tsx` `errors=0 warnings=55`, **exactly the `fd8dacecc` baseline** — measured by linting the base blob as a probe file in the same directory, not assumed.
- **`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`** — exit 0. Its verdict line: *"1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s) ... Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing, which is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate."*
- `check-changeset-fixed` / `check-changeset-no-major` / `check-control-bytes` — exit 0 each, verdict lines *"All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group."*, *"No changeset declares a `major` bump."*, *"check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 5803 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)."*
- Dependency closure built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`, exit 0), so none of the above is a false RED off an unbuilt tree.

## Bound of the reading, stated

- objectui `origin/main` at `fd8dacecc`; `@objectstack/spec` resolved 17.2.0 in a fresh worktree install.
- **No server was booted.** "The server refuses schema-invalid drafts" is read from `doSave`'s 422 handling and `clientValidation.ts`'s own header, not observed on the wire. "The server accepts malformed CEL" is cited from #4306's measurement, not re-run.
- History searched over #4306's body, its 3 comments and PR #4536's body — 18,601 characters. Ten probe terms (`zod`, `clientValidation`, `validateMetadataDraft`, `hasClientValidator`, `setIssues`, `schema validation`, `spec skew`, `skew`, `422`, `invalid_metadata`) returned **0 hits total**; five hot-control terms in the same pass over the same corpus returned 64 (`inspector` 53, `celPredicateField` 4, `perm.cel.saveBlocked` 4, `onLintChange` 2, `onBlockingIssuesChange` 1). The zero is a measurement. Independently, `ResourceEditPage.tsx` **at #4536's base commit** already imported and ran `validateMetadataDraft`, with a Save gate of `disabled={saving || (!createMode && !isDirty)}` — no validation term at all. The Zod validator was there and was not weighed.
- Not covered: any repo outside objectui; the framework's `/meta/types` response shape beyond the `required` array the cure reads; e2e or browser behaviour.

## Filed for triage, not addressed here

Card **#6982** — two of `clientValidation.ts`'s three spec-skew cures now rest on stale premises on 17.2.0: `FORWARD_COMPAT_FLOW_NODE_TYPES` is unreachable (node `type` is an open string), and `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES`' hold on `sharing_rule` was measured on 17.0.0-rc.5, whereas `SharingRuleSchema` now declares all 7 ADR-0010 envelope keys. Out of scope here: lifting that opt-out turns a client gate **on** for a security-metadata edit door. That card is open and unassigned; nothing in this PR addresses it.

## Not done here, on purpose

Gating Save on client Zod errors is **not** implemented, and the evidence above is why it should not be. Nothing was skipped, disabled or quarantined; no PR was marked ready and no auto-merge was enabled.
